system.hostCollection.title: Host collection onboarding
system.hostCollection.subtitle: Choose a path that fits your infrastructure. Sentinel queries a Prometheus-compatible backend; it does not deploy collectors.
system.hostCollection.catalogLoading: Reading supported onboarding paths from the Console…
system.hostCollection.catalogFailed: The server deployment guide could not be confirmed. The guidance below is informational, not a validated template.
system.hostCollection.collectorNotConfig: The Sentinel Runtime Collector advertised endpoint is not configured.
system.hostCollection.readiness.guide-on: Operational guidance only; no validated deployment template
system.hostCollection.boundary: Collectors discover and scrape host metrics; Prometheus stores and serves queries. The application Sentinel Collector is a separate reporting path and must not be used as the host monitoring source.
system.hostCollection.existing.title: Reuse an existing Prometheus-compatible stack
system.hostCollection.existing.descripti: For environments where a platform team already operates Prometheus, Thanos, or a compatible query service. Do not install duplicate exporters.
system.hostCollection.existing.step1: Confirm that the backend scrapes the target hosts and preserves stable instance identity and scrape-job labels.
system.hostCollection.existing.step2: Register the query URL, authentication, environment, and label mapping below; run connection and sample checks before saving as verified.
system.hostCollection.existing.step3: Open Real-time Monitoring and inspect real HOST samples and freshness. The collection path is usable only when samples are actually returned.
system.hostCollection.existing.availabil: The URL and credentials are used to query the backend; this does not deploy or modify scrape jobs.
system.hostCollection.linux.title: Add Linux hosts to Prometheus scraping
system.hostCollection.linux.description: Install an operations-approved node exporter on each Linux host and have Prometheus scrape its metrics endpoint.
system.hostCollection.linux.step1: Install the exporter from organization-approved packages with a pinned version and host baseline; expose its scrape port only to trusted collectors.
system.hostCollection.linux.step2: Configure Prometheus scrape targets with a stable, unique instance label per host; the scrape-job label must match the registered source.
system.hostCollection.linux.step3: Verify CPU, memory, and load samples for the host in Prometheus, then register the query backend below and run the sample check.
system.hostCollection.linux.availability: The server does not yet provide a version-pinned Linux deployment profile, so this is operational guidance, not a ready-to-run install command.
system.hostCollection.kubernetes.title: Discover Kubernetes nodes through cluster collection
system.hostCollection.kubernetes.descrip: Use a platform-approved node-exporter deployment in the cluster and scrape it through Prometheus Operator or existing scrape configuration.
system.hostCollection.kubernetes.step1: Have a cluster administrator review the DaemonSet, host mounts, permissions, security context, network policies, and exporter version; do not apply an unreviewed manifest.
system.hostCollection.kubernetes.step2: Configure Prometheus discovery and scraping, mapping each Kubernetes node to a stable unique instance label. Container metrics require a separate collection profile.
system.hostCollection.kubernetes.step3: Verify fresh HOST-scope samples in Prometheus, then register the query backend and check environment, scrape-job, and identity-label mappings.
system.hostCollection.kubernetes.availab: The server does not yet provide a version-pinned Kubernetes deployment profile; Sentinel will not connect to the cluster or install components remotely.
